chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about salat (prayer) during travel, and he said: “Do not perform salat (prayer) on the roadway; rather, move aside to its edges.”

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the state in which this ruling applies
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being asked about
key_terms.جَانِبَيْهَا: its two sides or edges, where one should move to pray
key_terms.لَا تُصَلِّ: do not pray, expressing the prohibition or disallowance here

ai.seo_question: Can you perform salat (prayer) on the road while traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding where salat (prayer) should be performed while traveling. It instructs that one should not pray on the main roadway itself, but instead move aside to its edges, indicating concern for propriety, safety, and avoiding obstruction.
